data.reasoning: Both models reviewed the executable and packaging files (PKGBUILD, hook, generate script, env template) and found them to be standard, safe AUR packaging for a Node.js application. The only discrepancy was an API error in the qwen model when processing the .SRCINFO metadata file, which incorrectly forced an 'inconclusive' overall verdict. The deepseek model successfully audited all files and correctly determined the package is safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is not substantive. The qwen model returned 'inconclusive' solely due to an HTTP 400 API error when attempting to audit the .SRCINFO file. The deepseek model successfully audited .SRCINFO and all other files, returning 'safe'. There is no actual security disagreement between the models' reasoning.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .SRCINFO due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400), resulting in an incomplete audit and an 'inconclusive' overall verdict.
learnings: The audit orchestrator should not fail the entire audit or return 'inconclusive' if a tool error (like an API timeout or 400 error) occurs on a non-executable metadata file (e.g., .SRCINFO) when all critical packaging files have been successfully audited and found safe.
Implement retry logic or graceful degradation for transient API errors on individual files so that a single metadata file failure doesn't block the final verdict.
